name: LP-MSPM33C321A LaunchPad development kit
sources: MSPM33C321x data sheet SLASFB6A (Rev. A, revised September 2026; features, supply currents, flash wait states); LaunchPad user guide SLAU969 (December 2025; Table 2-1 jumpers, section 2.3 J101, 2.8 NOR flash, 2.9 OLED, Figure 4-2 header pinout); TI product and tool pages; MSPM33 SDK 1.04.00.00 on this Mac. All read 2026-10-07.

columns.head: The chip: MSPM33C321A
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M33
Up to 160 million steps a second (160 MHz), with a floating-point unit, DSP instructions and TrustZone (a hardware wall between trusted and normal code)
Flash: 1 MB
Holds the program, in two banks that can swap for safe updates. Plus 32 kB of data flash for settings
RAM: 256 kB
Working memory. Eight times the LP-MSPM0G3507, so full graphics buffers and big models fit
Power: 3.3 V on this board
The chip accepts 1.71 to 3.6 V. Data sheet: 33.7 mA running CoreMark at 160 MHz, 8 µA in STANDBY

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: GPIO: up to 93
Plain on/off pins: LEDs, buttons, control lines
UART: 8 / SPI: 5 / I2C: up to 9
Serial text, fast buses for screens and memory, two-wire sensor buses (many pins can be any of the three)
ADC: 2
Two 12-bit converters, 9.4 million samples a second each, sampling at the same instant
Comparators: 2
Each with an 8-bit DAC; the two DACs can also drive a pin
Timers: 9
Up to 30 PWM outputs; two advanced timers for motors and power
Chip: security engines
AES-256 and SHA-256 engines, a public-key engine (ECC, RSA), a true random number generator, secure boot from ROM

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
XDS110 debug probe with EnergyTrace (current measurement), 0.91 inch 128 x 32 OLED, 8 MB QSPI NOR flash, RGB LED, red LED, 2 buttons, 100 mF super capacitor for the battery domain, mikroBUS socket
Headers
80-pin BoosterPack layout (J1 to J8) plus a mikroBUS socket
Not on the chip
No neural accelerator (NPU), no radio, no trig math unit
Watch out
Prototype kit in limited quantity. The out-of-box OLED demo is not in the SDK: back up flash and the NOR chip before writing anything
